rows.what_the_ink_shows: The identifiable right-margin mark near (1642,859) is a short dark vertically elongated stroke with a curved right side and a narrowing lower part, compatible with a comma rather than a round dot. It lies well to the right of the Z display. A different much smaller roundish speck is below the first B of that display, near (761,967). The page packet supplies no coordinates to establish which mark the prior crop showed. Both locations are visible together in crops/156-5_scan015_Q100020_all_context.jpg, box [505,784,1675,1058]. Also viewed the right-mark context crops/156-5_scan015_Q100020_context.jpg, box [1230,749,1672,1052], the enlarged right mark crops/156-5_scan015_Q100020.jpg, box [1518,784,1671,1002], and the different below-formula spot crops/156-5_scan015_Q100020_lower.jpg, box [685,929,830,1008].
rows.note: Q100020.R1: Retain the existing \margin{\unsure{.}} without adding a comma reading or deleting the mark. Decision b is used here for an unresolved optical interpretation, not an asserted author slip. The row’s round-speck/no-tail description does not match the identifiable compact curved right-margin stroke; it may instead describe the separate spot below the formula. Its exact target and whether the margin mark is non-ink or intentional punctuation cannot be established securely. The lower speck is a distinct locus and is not newly transcribed. Main-reader review of the all-context and right-margin closeup agreed to retain the original doubt. The exploratory left-margin crop was also viewed, but excessive local contrast makes it unsuitable as evidence and it is not used for the decision.
